content: 1. Form FDA 1572, also known as the Statement of Investigator, is a document that the investigator signs to provide specific information to the sponsor and to assure compliance with FDA regulations regarding the conduct of clinical investigations involving investigational drugs or biologics. 2. The purpose of Form FDA 1572 is twofold: first, to provide the sponsor with information about the investigator’s qualifications and the clinical site to ensure the investigator is qualified and the site is appropriate for the clinical investigation; second, to inform the investigator of their obligations and obtain their commitment to comply with FDA regulations. 3. Investigators must complete and sign Form FDA 1572 only after receiving sufficient information about the clinical investigation, including the protocol, the investigator’s brochure (if applicable), and relevant FDA regulations. By signing, the investigator affirms their qualifications and commits to adhering to FDA regulations. 4. Investigators are not required to be physicians. However, if the investigator is not a physician, a qualified physician or dentist should be listed as a sub-investigator to oversee trial-related medical or dental decisions. 5. The regulations do not specify minimum qualifications for investigators. Sponsors are responsible for selecting investigators who are appropriately qualified by training and experience to conduct the clinical investigation. 6. Form FDA 1572 does not need to be submitted to the FDA. Sponsors are required to collect the form from investigators but are not required to send it to the agency. 7. Updates to Form FDA 1572 are not required for changes such as the addition of sub-investigators or clinical research labs. Instead, these changes should be documented in the clinical study records and communicated to the sponsor for appropriate updates to the IND. 8. Investigators are not required to sign Form FDA 1572 for studies not conducted under an IND or for medical device studies. The form is only required for investigational drug and biologic studies conducted under an IND. 9. Sponsors are not required to conduct foreign clinical studies under an IND. However, if a foreign study is conducted under an IND, all FDA IND requirements must be met unless waived. 10. Investigators conducting foreign clinical studies under an IND must comply with FDA IND regulations, including signing Form FDA 1572. If local laws prohibit signing the form, the site should operate as a non-IND site. 11. Investigators conducting foreign clinical studies under an IND must comply with local laws and regulations in addition to FDA requirements. Sponsors are encouraged to obtain written statements from investigators acknowledging their commitment to comply with local laws. 12. FDA may grant waivers for certain IND requirements, such as IRB requirements, if alternative mechanisms for protecting human subjects are acceptable. Waiver requests should be submitted to the appropriate FDA review division. 13. Non-U.S. investigators in multinational studies conducted under an IND must comply with FDA IND requirements, including signing Form FDA 1572, unless the site is not included under the IND. 14. Multinational studies may include domestic sites under an IND and foreign sites not under an IND. Foreign sites not under the IND are not required to sign Form FDA 1572. 15. Sponsors can submit information from foreign clinical studies not conducted under an IND to support U.S. clinical investigations or marketing approval. 16. A new Form FDA 1572 does not need to be prepared or signed when the OMB expiration date has passed. 17. FDA recommends stapling the two-page Form FDA 1572 to ensure clarity about the form signed by the investigator. 18. Form FDA 1572 can be completed electronically or by hand. Typed forms are preferred for legibility. The completed form must be signed and dated by the investigator. 19. The investigator’s name on Form FDA 1572 should match their legal name. Titles, degrees, and professional qualifications may follow the legal name if desired. 20. The address entered in Section 1 of Form FDA 1572 should be where the investigator can be reached by mail or in person, typically their work or business address. 21. Co-investigators are not defined in FDA regulations. Each co-investigator must sign a separate Form FDA 1572. 22. Section 2 of Form FDA 1572 requires the investigator to attach a CV or other statement of qualifications to demonstrate their expertise in conducting the clinical investigation. 23. FDA regulations do not require CVs or statements of qualifications to be updated during a clinical study. 24. CVs do not need to be signed or dated. The investigator’s signature on Form FDA 1572 attests to the accuracy of the CV or statement of qualifications. 25. Section 3 of Form FDA 1572 should include the addresses of all locations where the investigation will be conducted and where test articles will be shipped, if different from the investigator’s address. 26. Section 3 identifies facilities where study activities will occur, including locations where subjects are seen, study procedures are performed, or clinical data is collected. 27. The names and addresses of all study sites should be listed in Section 3. If the protocol allows for test articles to be administered at subjects’ homes, these addresses do not need to be listed. 28. Section 4 of Form FDA 1572 identifies clinical laboratories or testing facilities directly contributing to or supporting the clinical study. 29. Only the primary laboratory needs to be listed in Section 4, provided it can trace samples to satellite or contract labs. 30. The IRB reviewing the clinical study does not need to be located at the research site, as long as it meets FDA requirements. 31. Section 6 of Form FDA 1572 should list sub-investigators who are part of the investigative team and make direct, significant contributions to the study data. 32. Hospital staff providing ancillary or intermittent care do not need to be listed individually in Section 6 unless they make significant contributions to the clinical data. 33. Pharmacists and research coordinators should be listed in Section 6 if they make direct, significant contributions to the study data. 34. Sub-investigators do not need to submit statements of qualifications. Sponsors are responsible for selecting qualified investigators. 35. Individuals listed in Section 6 must submit financial disclosure information to the sponsor, including information about their spouse and dependent children. 36. Section 7 of Form FDA 1572 should include the name and code number of all protocols under the IND that the investigator will conduct. 37. For a Phase 4 study, the investigator should identify the study as Phase 4 in Section 7 but does not need to mark boxes in Section 8. 38. Investigators may submit the full study protocol instead of an outline for Phase 2 or 3 clinical trials.
